question: A temporary alliance of groups or parties is called a ______.
solution:
**The correct answer is Coalition__.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** temporary alliance** of groups or parties is called a Coalition**. **
 
• The term also describes alliances between civil society organizations, such as labor unions, community organizations, and religious institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and constituent political units.
 
• A **coalition** is an **alliance of political parties** or groups that come together to form a government or to support a particular policy or agenda.
 
 
• Coalitions are usually formed when** no single party has a majority** in a legislative body.
 
 
 
• **Constituency** refers to a **geographical area **that is represented by an elected official.
 
 
• In electoral politics, a constituency is the** group of voters** within a specific geographic area who are eligible to vote for a particular candidate.
 
 
 
• **Veto** is a power that allows a person or group to **reject a decision or proposal** made by another person or group.
 
 
• In political systems, the power of veto is usually held by the **executive branch of government.**
